punctilious

/puhngk-TIL-ee-uhs/ - the stress falls on TIL · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Punctilious means carefully exact about rules and details of conduct.

The club's punctilious secretary reads the minutes aloud twice — once for content, once for commas.

Worked Example

The tea master's apprenticeship was a lesson in punctilious form: the bowl turned exactly twice, the whisk set down at the same angle every time, guests greeted in an order fixed by centuries of custom—and none of it optional.

Punctilious narrows 'careful' to the fine points of correct form—rules, courtesies, ceremony. A careful person double-checks the numbers; a punctilious one also knows which of the three forks this course requires.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

precise: Precise means exact in detail generally — a precise measurement, a precise answer — and carries no special interest in manners. Punctilious narrows exactness to conduct: rules, courtesies, ceremony, the fine points of correct form. An engineer can be precise about tolerances yet clueless about which fork the fish course requires; the punctilious never are.

meticulous: Meticulous means extremely careful and thorough about the details of any task — a meticulous proofreader misses nothing anywhere. Punctilious aims that care specifically at correct form: protocol, etiquette, the proper order of things. A meticulous editor checks every figure; a punctilious diplomat knows which flag outranks which.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

careless: letting details slip without noticing

slapdash: done hastily, with no regard for form

Where it sits · how minutely correctness is pursued — careful → exacting → punctilious

careful vs. punctilious: Careful stops far short of punctilious — careful covers ordinary, everyday attention.

exacting vs. punctilious: Exacting stops short of punctilious — the exacting demand high standards, while the punctilious honor every fine point of form and etiquette.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — punctili-

Root — punctili-: a fine point (Italian puntiglio, from Latin punctum, a point)

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: full of

Put it together

Put it together: Punctili- (a fine point) + -ous = full of fine points. Latin punctum, 'a point,' shrank into Italian puntiglio, 'a small point of honor or etiquette,' and English borrowed the bundle: the punctilious mind every small point of correct form, one dot at a time.

Use the root in a new word: punctuation

Use the root in a new word: punctuation: One stray comma of punctuation changed the whole contract's meaning.
